notes.meaning: Paul now turns to the practical part of his letter. He asks gently, as a brother, not as a boss. The Thessalonians were already living in a way that pleased God, and Paul wants them to keep growing in it "more and more." Holding on to the faith is not enough. Believers should keep growing in how they live.

Paul reminds them of the rules for living he taught while he was with them. These were not his own ideas. He gave them by the authority of the Lord Jesus. The apostles passed on what Christ commanded rather than making up rules of their own.

God wants his people to be holy. This is sometimes called "sanctification," which means being set apart for God and made pure. One clear part of this is staying away from sexual immorality, which covers every kind of sex outside marriage. This was badly needed in a culture where such sin was common and not even seen as wrong.

differ.view: John Wesley described the holiness God wants here as "entire holiness of heart and life," a full holiness that God works in the believer.

notes.meaning: Each believer must learn to control his own body, keeping it pure and treating it with honor. The body is like a vessel, a container, that holds the soul. It should not be ruled by its appetites. Giving the body over to sexual sin brings shame on it.

differ.view: Some older commentators read "vessel" as "wife," meaning each man should take his own wife and live with her in purity and honor.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars think "vessel" most likely means "body." A few suggest it is a polite way of speaking about the sexual organs.

notes.meaning: Believers must not be driven by lustful passion like the Gentiles (people who are not Jews and here do not know God). Such passion makes a person its slave. People who do not know God know no better. Christians do know him, so they should live differently.

Sexual sin is also a wrong done to other people. Taking another man's wife, for example, cheats a brother and harms a marriage. Paul speaks politely of "this matter" but the meaning is clear. God will punish such sins, even when no one else finds out.

differ.view: Some read this verse more broadly, as a warning against cheating, oppressing, or taking advantage of anyone in any kind of dealing.

notes.meaning: When God called us to follow him, it was never so we could live impure lives. He called us to holiness. This sums up the whole passage and points back to verse 3.

Some might brush off these rules because they came from a man. But Paul says they are God's commands, so rejecting them means rejecting God. God gives his Holy Spirit to his people. The Spirit helps them see what is true and gives them strength to live holy lives.

Paul does not need to say much about love for fellow believers. God himself, by his Spirit, had already taught them to love one another. Everyone God truly teaches learns this lesson. The Spirit's teaching goes deeper than any human teacher's.
Their love reached beyond their own city to believers all over Macedonia, the region around them. Paul praises this, but he still urges them to grow more. No one this side of heaven loves perfectly.

Paul says to make it your ambition to live a calm, peaceful life. Mind your own affairs instead of meddling in others' business, and work to earn your living. It seems some had stopped working, perhaps because they expected Jesus to return soon, and were leaning on others. Honest, quiet work earns the respect of outsiders, keeps believers from depending on others, and shows that faith does not make people lazy.

Some believers in Thessalonica had died, and their friends were troubled. They may have feared the dead would miss out when Christ returns. Paul calls death "sleep" because the body rests until it is raised again. Grieving is not wrong, and Jesus himself wept. But Christians should not grieve like people who have no hope of life after death.

Our hope rests on what we believe: Jesus died and rose again. Believers are joined to Jesus, so what happened to him will happen to them. God will raise those who died trusting in Jesus and bring them with him. Their bond with Christ is stronger than death.

Paul speaks with the Lord's own authority. Believers still alive when Jesus returns will not go ahead of those who have died. When he says "we," Paul speaks as one of the whole family of believers in every age. He was not promising that Jesus would come in his own lifetime. The point is that every believer should live ready, as if the Lord could come at any time.

differ.view: Some believe the "we" shows Paul fully expected to be alive himself to meet the Lord.

notes.meaning: Jesus himself, not a messenger, will come down from heaven, just as he went up. His coming will be grand and loud, with a shout of command, the voice of an archangel (a chief angel), and God's trumpet calling his people together. Then the believers who have died will rise first. They will not be left out.

After the dead rise, believers still alive will be changed in an instant. Together with the raised dead, they will be caught up in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. They do not stay in the air. The best part is that they will be with the Lord forever and never be parted again.

differ.view: Some believe this "rapture" (from the Latin word for "caught up") could happen at any moment and is separate from Christ's later return to earth. On this view, he first comes for his people and takes them away before the tribulation, a time of great trouble, and later comes back with them.
Others believe this describes Christ's one visible return after the tribulation. Believers rise to meet him and then come back to earth with him.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching accepts the event in this verse but sees it as part of Christ's one glorious coming at the end of time, with the resurrection and judgment. It rejects the idea of a secret, early removal of believers as a newer idea from the 1800s.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: The word for "meet" was used for a group going out to welcome an important visitor and walk him back into the city.

notes.meaning: Paul tells them to use these truths to comfort each other. Believers who died will not stay in the grave and will not miss out. All of God's people will be with the Lord forever. Believers should help carry one another's sorrow, not just look for comfort for themselves.
